result:
There is a particular quiet that arrives just before dawn. It is not the quiet of emptiness, but of preparation—the world holding its breath before beginning again.

Streetlights glow without confidence. Windows remain dark. Somewhere, a delivery truck sighs at the curb, and a bird tests a single note, as if asking whether morning is ready.

Most beginnings are like this. They do not announce themselves with trumpets or clean certainty. They emerge gradually: an idea scribbled in the margin, an apology rehearsed but not yet spoken, a suitcase left open on the bed. We often imagine that change begins with courage, but more often it begins with attention. We notice that something no longer fits. We notice what keeps returning to our thoughts. We notice the door.

Then comes the smallest possible movement.

A hand reaches for the handle.  
A page turns.  
The sky becomes, almost imperceptibly, blue.
